title: Create a usability evidence and design decision review workspace
summary: A designer or developer can capture a task, expected outcome, observed interaction evidence, accessibility notes, decision, proposal, and implemented result around a Board or screen without turning Studio into surveillance.
acceptance_criteria: The experience starts from an explicit local state and explains source, revision/freshness, confidence, privacy scope, and why the app is requesting attention or feedback.
Unavailable, stale, partial, failed, blocked, conflicted, revoked, deleted, unsupported, and unknown states are semantically distinct from healthy or completed state.
The user can inspect the exact proposed consequence before accepting a correction, restore, personalization change, retry, support export, deletion, or external handoff.
Feedback and learning are explicit, editable, deletable, and separated into factual correction, preference, outcome, interruption, uncertainty, and optional narrative.
The app explains which evidence will change future behavior and provides reset, disable, exclude-once, and revert controls; no hidden personalization is introduced.
Sparse, stale, contradictory, or low-confidence evidence produces a neutral or conservative result rather than fabricated certainty or forced adaptation.
Every irreversible or externally visible action has separate confirmation, stable operation/receipt identity, progress state, retry behavior, and honest partial-success handling.
Offline use, interruption, app restart, source revision change, missing consumer, duplicate delivery, and conflicting local edits recover deterministically and remain visible.
A privacy-safe support package can be previewed and exported only on explicit request; raw secrets and unrelated personal data are never collected simply because the surface exists.
The experience remains fully useful without HumbleControl; optional Trust Center projection receives minimal typed state rather than private domain payloads.
Keyboard and assistive navigation, scalable type, non-color status cues, reduced-motion behavior, and accessible explanations are verified.
All visible copy uses the repository localization source of truth; dates, numbers, units, currency, and relative time are locale-aware.
Telemetry is purpose-limited and coarse: it records state or failure class and explicit feedback posture, not sensitive narrative, raw artifacts, full paths/URLs, or hidden cross-app identity.
Deterministic tests cover happy path, cancellation, opt-out, correction, stale evidence, offline, duplicate, partial, conflict, unsupported state, recovery, and deletion/revocation where relevant.
Evidence may include user-authored notes, task timing ranges, selected screenshots, focus/navigation traces, accessibility findings, and explicit ratings; recording is opt-in and scope-previewed.
The workspace separates observed evidence, interpretation, hypothesis, design decision, accepted tradeoff, proposal, implementation receipt, and follow-up result.
A design decision can be superseded or rejected while retaining rationale and can generate a qualified HumbleControl Finding or Studio proposal only after review.
The strongest repository-native tests, builds, visual/runtime/accessibility evidence, contract checks, and diff hygiene pass with zero app-owned warnings.

agent_notes: Portfolio Stewardship Wave 4; signature trust, recovery, and transparent-learning user journey.
Estimated effort: L, approximately 8-20 focused working hours after prerequisites; split only when evidence proves a stable smaller boundary.
Implementation risk: medium-high because lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, release, or learning semantics can affect durable user trust.
Non-scope: Do not record screen/audio by default, create hidden analytics, rank individual users, or auto-accept design changes from a metric.
Alternative considered and rejected: Attach comments to screenshots — comments alone do not preserve task, observation, interpretation, decision, implementation, and follow-up lineage.
Do not weaken the application, fabricate evidence, convert unavailable data to success, hide warnings, broaden consent, or centralize domain ownership to satisfy this ticket.
Close only after repository-native tests/builds, fixture and migration evidence, accessibility/privacy review where applicable, and zero app-owned warnings.
Wave 8 portfolio reassessment: retain; priority band next. Data lifecycle, recovery, supportability, and transparent learning are professional product requirements.
Wave 10 final rationalization: retain-operational; portfolio band later. Lifecycle, recovery, support, and transparent feedback remain professional operations work.
Wave 11 execution reconciliation: `supporting-input`. Use the Wave 11 implementation program as the delivery entry point while preserving this ticket's evidence and intent.

Wave 12 deep reassessment: decision `retain-supporting`, relevance `next`, current priority `medium`, execution gate `sequence behind current correctness and the bounded delivery program`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and transparent learning remain professional requirements.
Wave 13 human-validation reassessment: `retain-operational-input` / `next` / priority `medium`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and feedback are required for trustworthy beta use.

Final Wave 14 validity review: `valid`; publication `publish-after-fresh-reconciliation`; implementation sequence `after-sudoku`. Lifecycle, privacy, recovery, support, and feedback are required for trustworthy beta use.
